text: An NCC parade is going at a uniform speed of $9\mathrm{km}/\mathrm{h}$ under a mango tree on which a monkey is sitting at a height of $19.6\mathrm{m}$. At any particular instant, the monkey drops a mango. A cadet will receive the mango whose distance from the tree at time of drop is: (Given $g=9.8\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
An NCC parade is moving at a steady speed of 9 km/h under a mango tree where a monkey is perched at a height of 19.6 meters. Suddenly, the monkey drops a mango. To determine which cadet will catch the mango, we need to calculate the distance of the cadet from the tree at the moment the mango is dropped, considering the acceleration due to gravity $g=9.8\text{m/s}^{2}$.

First, we use the formula to find the time $t$ it takes for the mango to fall:

$H=\frac{1}{2}gt^{2}$

Substituting the given values:

$19.6=4.9t^{2}$

Solving for $t$:

$t^{2}=\frac{19.6}{4.9}$

$t^{2}=4$

$t=2\text{\sec }$

Next, we need to find the distance $D$ the cadet travels in these 2 seconds:

$D=\text{speed}\times \text{time}$

Since the speed is given in km/h, we first convert it to m/s:

$9~\text{km/h}=9\times \frac{1000}{3600}\text{m/s}=2.5\text{m/s}$

So, the distance covered by the cadet is:

$D=2.5\text{m/s}\times 2\text{\sec }=5\text{m}$

Thus, the cadet who is 5 meters away from the tree at the moment the mango is dropped will catch the mango.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift

text: If the radius of earth shrinks by $2%$ while its mass remains same. The acceleration due to gravity on the earth's surface will approximately :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The acceleration due to gravity (g) on the surface of a planet is given by the formula:

$g=\frac{GM}{R^{2}}$

where:

G is the gravitational constant,
M is the mass of the planet,
R is the radius of the planet.

If the radius of the Earth shrinks by 2% but its mass remains the same, the new acceleration due to gravity (g') will be:

$g^{'}=\frac{GM}{(0.98R)^{2}}=\frac{GM}{0.9604R^{2}}=\frac{g}{0.9604}$

This implies that g' is approximately 1.0412 times g, or an increase of approximately 4.12%.

Therefore, the acceleration due to gravity on the Earth's surface will approximately increase by 4%.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift

solution.body:
Let the rod have length $l$ and mass $m=λl$, with $λ=0.45\text{kg m}^{-1}$. The current in the rod is horizontal and the field is vertical, so the magnetic force $F=ilB$ is horizontal and perpendicular to the rod, pushing it towards the incline.

The plane is smooth, so the normal reaction takes the components perpendicular to the plane, and only the components along the incline must balance:

$ilB\cos 45^{\circ }=mg\sin 45^{\circ }\Rightarrow i=\dfrac{mg\tan 45^{\circ }}{lB}=\dfrac{λg}{B}$

The length cancels, so only the linear density is needed:

$i=\dfrac{0.45\times 10}{0.15}=30\text{A}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).

The equation of current in a purely inductive circuit is $5\sin (49πt-30^{\circ })$. If the inductance is $30\quad \mathrm{mH}$ then the equation for the voltage across the inductor, will be :

$\{~$ Let $\left. π=\frac{22}{7}\right \}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In a purely inductive circuit the voltage leads the current by $90^{\circ }$, and its amplitude is $V_{0}=I_{0}ωL$.


[IMG]

Here $I_{0}=5\text{A}$, $ω=49π\text{rad s}^{-1}$ and $L=30\text{mH}=0.03\text{H}$, so

$V_{0}=5\times 49\times \frac{22}{7}\times 0.03=5\times 154\times 0.03=23.1\text{V}$

Adding $90^{\circ }$ to the phase of the current,

$V=23.1\sin (49πt-30^{\circ }+90^{\circ })=23.1\sin (49πt+60^{\circ })$

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text:
The equation $λ=\frac{1.227}{x}\mathrm{nm}$ can be used to find the de-Brogli wavelength of an electron. In this equation $x$ stands for :

Where

$\mathrm{m}=$ mass of electron

$\mathrm{P}=$ momentum of electron

$\mathrm{K}=$ Kinetic energy of electron

$\mathrm{V}=$ Accelerating potential in volts for electron
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The de Broglie wavelength of a particle can be expressed as:

$λ=\frac{h}{p}$

where:

$h$ is Planck's constant, and
$p$ is the momentum of the particle.

For an electron accelerated through a potential difference of $V$ volts, its kinetic energy $K$ is given by:

$K=eV$

where $e$ is the charge of an electron.

The electron's momentum can be expressed in terms of its kinetic energy as:

$p=\sqrt{2mK}$

where $m$ is the mass of the electron.

Substituting this into the de Broglie wavelength equation, we get:

$λ=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}$

Comparing this with the given equation $λ=\frac{1.227}{x}nm$, we see that $x$ must correspond to:

$x=\sqrt{2mK}$

Since $K=eV$, we can substitute this into our expression for $x$ to get:

$x=\sqrt{2meV}=\sqrt{V}$

where we've used the fact that the mass and charge of an electron are constants.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift

text: Identify the solar cell characteristics from the following options :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A solar cell is a p-n junction that generates an emf when light falls on it; no external bias is applied, and the photocurrent flows through the junction from n to p, opposite to the forward current of a diode.

Its I-V characteristic therefore lies in the fourth quadrant: it meets the V-axis at the open-circuit voltage $V_{oc}$ and the I-axis at the short-circuit current $-I_{sc}$. This is the curve in graph (B).

Graph (A) is the forward characteristic of an ordinary p-n diode, (C) is the straight line of an ohmic conductor, and (D) is a diode characteristic with reverse breakdown (Zener diode).

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift

text: The frequencies at which the current amplitude in an LCR series circuit becomes $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ times its maximum value, are $212\mathrm{rad}\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ and $232\mathrm{rad}\mathrm{s}^{-1}$. The value of resistance in the circuit is $R=5\Omega$. The self inductance in the circuit is $__________$ $\mathrm{mH}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The current amplitude $I_{0}=\dfrac{V_{0}}{Z}$ is maximum, $\dfrac{V_{0}}{R}$, at resonance. It becomes $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ of the maximum when $Z=\sqrt{2}R$, that is when $|X_{L}-X_{C}|=R$.

Below resonance ($ω_{1}=212\text{rad s}^{-1}$) $X_{C}>X_{L}$, and above resonance ($ω_{2}=232\text{rad s}^{-1}$) $X_{L}>X_{C}$:

$\dfrac{1}{ω_{1}C}-ω_{1}L=R,ω_{2}L-\dfrac{1}{ω_{2}C}=R$

Equating the two left sides gives $\dfrac{1}{C}\left (\dfrac{1}{ω_{1}}+\dfrac{1}{ω_{2}}\right )=L(ω_{1}+ω_{2})$, so $\dfrac{1}{C}=ω_{1}ω_{2}L$ and $\dfrac{1}{ω_{2}C}=ω_{1}L$.

Substituting in the second equation:

$(ω_{2}-ω_{1})L=R\Rightarrow L=\dfrac{R}{ω_{2}-ω_{1}}=\dfrac{5}{232-212}=0.25\text{H}=250\text{mH}$

Hence, the answer is 250.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift
